name: Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy

criteria.description: Transient hypokinesis, akinesis, or dyskinesis of the left ventricular mid segments with or without apical involvement
Absence of obstructive coronary disease or angiographic evidence of acute plaque rupture
New electrocardiographic abnormalities (ST-segment elevation and/or T-wave inversion) or modest elevation in cardiac troponin

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All major criteria plus exclusion of myocarditis and pheochromocytoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires transient left ventricular dysfunction with typical wall motion abnormalities and exclusion of obstructive coronary artery disease.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic imaging finding on echocardiogram or ventriculography

laboratory: Mildly elevated cardiac troponin I or T
Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP
imaging: Echocardiogram showing apical ballooning and left ventricular dysfunction
Coronary angiography showing absence of obstructive coronary artery disease
Cardiac MRI excluding myocarditis and confirming wall motion abnormalities
other: Electrocardiogram with ST-segment elevation or T-wave inversion
Transient nature of left ventricular dysfunction with recovery within days to weeks

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of obstructive coronary artery disease on angiography
Inflammatory infiltrates on cardiac MRI or biopsy
Recurrent episodes triggered by catecholamine surges

redFlags: Sudden onset chest pain with ECG changes mimicking myocardial infarction
references: Prasad A, Lerman A, Rihal CS. Apical ballooning syndrome (Tako-Tsubo or stress cardiomyopathy): a mimic of acute myocardial infarction. Am Heart J. 2008;155(3):408-417.
Templin C, Ghadri JR, Diekmann J, et al. Clinical features and outcomes of Takotsubo (stress) cardiomyopathy. N Engl J Med. 2015;373(10):929-938.
Mayo Clinic Diagnostic Criteria for Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy. Mayo Clinic Proceedings. 2008.
